newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK PUBLIC PETROLEUM(DEP) LOWERS GASOLINE PRICES.
newsitem.headline: GREEK PUBLIC PETROLEUM(DEP) LOWERS GASOLINE PRICES.

text.p: Greece's Public Petroleum Corporation (DEP) will cut gasoline prices by 1.2 drachmas per litre, effective on Thursday.
Transport diesel and heating oil prices will go up by 1.8 and 2.0 drachmas per litre respectively, DEP said.

The price adjustments come after higher world gasoline prices, up by $10.4 per metric tonne, higher transport diesel prices, up by $3.3 per metric tonne, higher heating oil prices, up by $4.1 per metric tonne, and a firmer dollar/drachma, up 4.51 drachmas, it said.

Despite higher international prices and a higher dollar/drachma rate, gasoline prices were lowered folloowing a government decision to slash consumption tax on petrol by 4.0 drachmas per litre for a two-month period ending September 30.
The government also imposed upper limits on gasoline prices outside Athens and Thessaloniki. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
